name: Chala
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Gur language of Ghana; Glottolog lists only wordlist/subclassification refs (Manessy 1969, Kleinewillinghofer 1997); no phonology found online

sources.citation: Abdul-Latif, Issaka Razak. 2025. Aspects of the phonology of Bogoŋ. MA thesis, Memorial University of Newfoundland (supervisors Sara J. Mackenzie, Douglas Wharram). vii+88 pp. DOI 10.48336/pn1t-jg29; https://hdl.handle.net/20.500.14783/12829
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: the word 'stress' never occurs for Bogoŋ (only in a Ladefoged quotation, p. 17ff.). Reports (pp. 4-5, after Kleinewillinghöfer 2022) that all vowels and syllabic nasals carry a pitch tone: high, low, falling or rising; p. 44 syllabic nasals bear tone; p. 81 tone explicitly excluded from the study for lack of data. Chapters cover phoneme inventory, syllable structure (CV, CVV, CVC, CCV, V, C), assimilation, vowel reduction, ATR harmony; no suprasegmental chapter.

sources.citation: Chan, Eugene (ed.), Numeral systems of the world's languages: Chala / Bogoŋ (data from Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer, 4 July 2008). https://lingweb.eva.mpg.de/channumerals/Chala.htm
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tone-marked numerals only (e.g. -nʊ́ŋ 'five', ŋkúó 'twenty'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page chal1269; Wikipedia (en, de) 'Chala language'; Wikidata Q35190; daybreakgh.org 'History of the Chala'
sources.note: Names (Cala, Cãla, Tsa, Tschala, Tshala, Bogoŋ), classification, location (Odomi, Keri, Agou, Kabiti in Nkwanta South; Jadigbe near Kpandai), ~3,000 (2003 GILLBT) ethnic, fluent speakers a few hundred; no phonology.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2000. The noun classification of Cala (Bogoŋ) - a case of contact-induced change. In A. Meißner & A. Storch (eds), Nominal classification in African languages (FAB 12), 37-68. Köln: Köppe.

sources.note: Main published description of Cala morphology; may carry a preliminary phonology/tone note with tone-marked data. Köppe sells the volume as PDF; Academia copy needs login.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2022. How to read and write Bogoŋ: the language of the Chala people. A phonological introduction to publications in/on Bogoŋ language. (unpublished; Bogoŋ Documentation Committee / author)

sources.note: The only first-hand phonological description of Chala; source of the tone statement (H, L, falling, rising on all vowels and syllabic nasals); an orthography guide might also say whether stress/prominence is written or exists. Cited in Abdul-Latif 2025 pp. 4, 8-11.
